summary.intent: Win the START Hack Munich Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" by analyzing Soony's confidential supply data, then building a deployed alert/recheck-and-act agent product (Today flow, routines, voice, email) ready for the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses launch despite an "all ok" plan and built a working app on branch jonas/today-flow: Today decision flow with email review, paper check, source anchoring, routines with a When/Then/Always diagram, two-step voice decisions, and Plan as an overview. 221 tests passed and the final Plan overview commit was in progress.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Files get replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256 checksums, not filenames.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, state, design); .env holds the token and is gitignored while .env.example is committed.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md require claiming tasks in PROGRESS.md, Entire checks before pushing, and asking before every push, PR or paid action.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, so 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint' is normal for read-only turns.
Approving a decision on real data sends real supplier emails, so checks and screenshots must mock all non-GET requests.
New routines default to 'ask' trust mode, and existing routines keep their mode. Legacy code-only routines have no recipe and cannot be drawn as a diagram.
Commit conventions: author josteng, no em dashes, no attribution trailers.

code.finding: Voice decisions now need prepare_decision, which returns a one-time token (TTL 600 s, stored in voice_tokens.json), then decide with token and confirmed. This stops the model from deciding in the same turn it announces the action.
forToday must never borrow another card's stop time. It uses ed.stops_at only if breaks_first_card equals the card, otherwise card.runs_dry, otherwise null.
The reader puts the part number in `item` or `supplier_part_no` rather than material_id, so a fallback key was needed. This took the game-card gap from 34,800 to 6,800.
build_strip attributes the edition stop to the limiting card (most copies at risk, then level), which fixed the misattributed 'Standard stopped' sentence.

workflow: Run a subagent to cross-check bulk documents (200 order confirmations and 59 scans) while the main thread reads the rest; it found the 80,000 vs 8,000 art-book overbooking.
Split UI work among parallel builders with disjoint file ownership and relay changes with SendMessage; the main thread builds, tests, screenshots and commits.
Verify UI live with Playwright screenshots against real data in view-only mode.
Check for doc edits by others (read before update) before rewriting shared artifact sections.

friction: The portal token was initially empty, which blocked data access (401) until it was set.
Hackathon design was rejected repeatedly as cluttered or unprofessional before settling on the minimal Sunday flow.
The UI offered Undo for emails already sent, which was misleading.
Voice assistant announced it would outline the action and then just decided, jumping the UI to 'Done'.
Three tests broke when decide began requiring a token, because they called decide directly.
Legacy test routines had no diagram and one failed on old code.
Builder files temporarily did not compile, blocking a live rebuild.
A stray .vite/ cache folder appeared in the repo root.
The Karton Nowak sleeve and art-book offers contradicted their own downtime notice.
